entry_json.avoid: In the IELTS Writing test there is no time for a full draft; plan briefly and write once.

entry_json.definition: to pull something heavy along the ground with effort; or to move an item on a screen with the mouse

contexts.text: I had to drag my suitcase up four flights of stairs because the lift was broken.
Users simply drag the icon onto the desktop, which removes the need for training.

confusables.difference: Pull is the neutral verb and says nothing about weight. Drag adds that the object is heavy and stays on the ground.

entry_json.definition: sudden, very great and often surprising; or connected with the theatre
entry_json.own_context_sentence: There was a dramatic fall in air pollution during the months when traffic stopped.

The changes to the timetable were dramatic and not popular.

contexts.text: The graph shows a dramatic increase in mobile use after 2010.
The changes at work were pretty dramatic, and not everyone coped.

confusables.difference: Significant means large enough to matter. Dramatic means large and sudden enough to surprise, so a slow steady rise can be significant but not dramatic.

entry_json.avoid: In Task 1, dramatic should be reserved for genuinely steep changes; using it for every movement makes the report unreliable.

entry_json.definition: wearing clothes, or wearing a particular kind of clothes
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Working from home, I sometimes forget to get dressed properly before a video call.

contexts.text: Working from home, I sometimes forget to get dressed properly before a video call.
Staff who are smartly dressed are still judged more competent, fairly or not.

confusables.difference: Wearing takes the clothes as its object: wearing a coat. Dressed takes in: dressed in a coat. Mixing them produces "dressed a coat", which is wrong.

entry_json.definition: a musical instrument that you hit with sticks or your hands; also a large round container
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Learning the drums taught me more about patience than any school subject.

Chemicals are shipped in steel drums that must be sealed properly.

contexts.text: He plays the drums in a band at weekends.
Chemicals are shipped in steel drums that must be sealed properly.

confusables.difference: Percussion is the whole family of instruments you strike. A drum is one of them.

entry_json.definition: having drunk too much alcohol, so that you cannot control your behaviour

contexts.text: Drunk driving fell sharply once the penalties were made automatic.
He was too drunk to remember the conversation the next day.

confusables.difference: Drank is the past simple, drunk the past participle and the adjective: "he drank too much" and "he was drunk".

entry_json.avoid: Do not write "he has drunk" when you mean he is drunk; the perfect tense means he consumed something.

entry_json.definition: expected to happen or arrive at a particular time; or owed as a payment

entry_json.definition: very fine dry powder that collects on surfaces or floats in the air

contexts.text: Fine dust from construction sites is a serious problem for people with asthma.
There was a thick layer of dust on everything in the room.

confusables.difference: Sand is much coarser and stays on the ground. Dust is fine enough to float in the air and to be breathed in.

entry_json.definition: something you must do because it is right or because it is part of your job; also a tax on goods
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Parents have a duty to make sure their children attend school.

contexts.text: Parents have a duty to make sure their children attend school.
The nurse on duty explained everything really clearly.

confusables.difference: Responsibility is broad and can be chosen. A duty is imposed by a role, a law or a moral rule, so it sounds stronger and less optional.

entry_json.definition: a sudden violent shaking of the ground
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Building codes matter far more than warning systems once an earthquake begins.

contexts.text: Building codes matter far more than warning systems once an earthquake begins.

entry_json.definition: in or from the east of a place
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Rainfall is much higher in the eastern half of the country than in the west.

Eastern Europe saw rapid change in the 1990s.

contexts.text: Rainfall is much higher in the eastern half of the country than in the west.
The eastern side of the city has the older housing stock.

entry_json.avoid: Do not write "in the east part"; use the eastern part or in the east of the country.

entry_json.definition: connected with the economy, or with trade, industry and money
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The economic case for investing in public transport is strong even before you count the environmental benefits.

Many migrants move for economic reasons rather than political ones.

contexts.text: Economic growth has slowed for the third year running.

entry_json.definition: the system by which a country's money, industry and trade are organised
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The local economy still depends on a single industry, which makes it fragile.
example_sentences: The economy grew by two per cent last year.

contexts.text: Tourism is now the largest sector of the island's economy.
The local economy still depends on a single industry, which makes it fragile.

confusables.difference: Economics is the academic subject. The economy is the real system of production and money in a country.

entry_json.avoid: The economy normally takes the: "the economy is growing", not "economy is growing".

entry_json.definition: the outside limit of an object, surface or area
entry_json.own_context_sentence: New housing keeps appearing on the edge of the city while the centre empties.

Careful editing gives one application the edge over another.

contexts.text: New housing keeps appearing on the edge of the city while the centre empties.
We live right on the edge of town, so the countryside starts at the end of our road.

confusables.difference: A border is the official line between countries or regions. An edge is the physical limit of any object or area.

entry_json.avoid: Use on the edge of, not "in the edge of".

entry_json.definition: to prepare a piece of writing, film or recording by correcting it and deciding what to include
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Learning to edit my own writing improved my marks more than learning new words did.
example_sentences: She edits the department newsletter in her own time.
The footage was edited down from six hours to twenty minutes.

contexts.text: Learning to edit my own writing improved my marks more than learning new words did.
The footage was edited down from six hours to twenty minutes.

confusables.difference: Correct only fixes mistakes. Edit also cuts, reorders and reshapes, so a well-edited text may have had nothing wrong with it.

entry_json.avoid: Edit does not double the t: edited, editing.

entry_json.definition: one of the printings of a book or newspaper, or one broadcast of a regular programme
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Check that you are using the third edition, because the chapter numbering changed.
example_sentences: The paperback edition costs half as much as the hardback.
The evening edition carried a longer version of the story.

contexts.text: Check that you are using the third edition, because the chapter numbering changed.
The revised edition includes data collected after 2018.

confusables.difference: A version can differ in content or language and applies to software, songs and stories. An edition is a specific printing or issue of a published work.
A copy is one physical book; an edition is the whole batch printed with the same content.

entry_json.avoid: Do not confuse edition with addition; they sound similar but mean entirely different things.

entry_json.definition: a person who prepares written work or film for publication, or who is in charge of a newspaper
entry_json.own_context_sentence: A good editor removes a third of your words and improves the argument.
example_sentences: She worked as an editor at a small publishing house.
The letter was addressed to the editor of the local paper.

contexts.text: A good editor removes a third of your words and improves the argument.
Letters to the editor remain one of the few open channels for public complaint.

confusables.difference: The author writes the text. The editor shapes and corrects what somebody else wrote.
The publisher is the company that produces and sells the book; the editor is a person who works on the text.

entry_json.avoid: Editor has -or, not -er, at the end.

entry_json.definition: to teach somebody over a period of time, especially at a school or college, or to give people information about something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Campaigns that educate the public about recycling work better than fines.

I was educated at a state school in the north of the city.

confusables.difference: Teach is what happens in a single lesson or on a single subject. Educate covers a whole formal process over years, or informing a whole population.

entry_json.avoid: Use be educated at a school and educated in a subject, not "educated from a school".

entry_json.definition: having received education, especially to a high level
entry_json.own_context_sentence: A well-educated workforce attracts investment more reliably than low taxes do.

I can only make an educated guess about next year's figures.

contexts.text: A well-educated workforce attracts investment more reliably than low taxes do.
I can only make an educated guess about next year's figures.

confusables.difference: Intelligent is natural ability. Educated is the result of schooling, and the two do not always go together.

entry_json.avoid: Hyphenate before a noun: a well-educated workforce, but the workforce is well educated.

entry_json.definition: connected with education, or providing something useful to learn
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Educational opportunities still depend heavily on where a child happens to be born.
example_sentences: The museum runs educational programmes for local schools.
The trip was genuinely educational rather than just a day out.

contexts.text: Educational opportunities still depend heavily on where a child happens to be born.
The trip was genuinely educational rather than just a day out.

confusables.difference: Academic means connected with study and research, and often contrasts with practical. Educational simply means concerning education or teaching you something.

entry_json.avoid: The noun is education; do not write "the educational of children".

entry_json.definition: producing the result that was intended
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Congestion charges have proved more effective than appeals to drivers' conscience.

The treatment is effective in most cases if it is started early.

contexts.text: Congestion charges have proved more effective than appeals to drivers' conscience.
Regular short revision sessions are more effective than one long one.

confusables.difference: Effective asks whether it works. Efficient asks whether it works without wasting time or money. A bulldozer is an effective way to open a tin but not an efficient one.

entry_json.avoid: Use effective in doing something or effective at doing something, not "effective to do".

entry_json.definition: in a way that produces the intended result; or used to say what the real situation amounts to
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Money spent early is used more effectively than money spent after the damage is done.

contexts.text: Removing the last bus effectively cuts the village off after seven o'clock.
I learned to manage my time more effectively during my final year.

confusables.difference: Efficiently means with little waste of time or resources. Effectively means the aim was achieved. A team can work efficiently on the wrong task.

entry_json.definition: doing something well without wasting time, money or energy
entry_json.own_context_sentence: An efficient rail network takes more cars off the road than any advertising campaign.
example_sentences: Modern boilers are far more efficient than those installed in the 1990s.
She is a quiet but extremely efficient administrator.

contexts.text: Modern boilers are far more efficient than those installed in the 1990s.
She is a quiet but extremely efficient administrator.

confusables.difference: Effective means it achieves the aim; efficient means it achieves it cheaply or quickly. Say which one you mean, because the two can point in opposite directions.

entry_json.definition: physical or mental energy needed to do something, or an attempt to do it
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Learning a language takes sustained effort rather than occasional bursts of enthusiasm.

entry_json.avoid: Fur is uncountable: not "furs" unless you mean fur garments.

entry_json.definition: to obtain or achieve something useful, or to gradually get more of something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Volunteering is one of the few ways to gain experience before you have any.
example_sentences: The party gained twelve seats at the last election.

contexts.text: The party gained twelve seats at the last election.

confusables.difference: Earn means receiving something in return for work, usually money. Gain is broader and covers experience, weight, speed and support.
Win requires a contest with an opponent. You gain a place at university, but you win a competition.

entry_json.avoid: Gain is transitive: "she gained experience", not "she gained" alone. Gain weight is neutral; put on weight is the spoken form.

entry_json.definition: an organised group of criminals, or a group of young people who spend time together and often cause trouble
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Youth centres are closed on cost grounds and gang membership rises soon afterwards.
example_sentences: The police broke up a gang that had been stealing from building sites.

confusables.difference: Group is entirely neutral. Gang carries a strong suggestion of crime or trouble, so calling your friends a gang is informal and jokey at best.
A team works together towards a shared goal, usually legitimate. A gang is bound by loyalty and often by crime.

entry_json.avoid: Do not use gang for a study group or a set of colleagues in formal writing; the negative sense dominates.
